items.q: The Arabic name for poetry in praise of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
The Companion poet for whom our Beloved Prophet ﷺ set up a minbar in the mosque to answer for him in verse.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ prayed that this one, the Holy Spirit, would support Hassan ibn Thabit ﵁.
The most famous poem of praise by al-Busiri ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, known by the name of a cloak.
The full title of al-Busiri's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ Burdah begins "al-Kawakib al-Durriyyah", meaning this.
The poem of the Companion Ka'b ibn Zuhayr ﵁, recited before our Beloved Prophet ﷺ, which opens "Banat Su'ad".
The words "Tala'a al-badru 'alayna" are linked in a weak report with our Beloved Prophet's ﷺ arrival in this city.

items.q: The Arabic word for a long poem with one rhyme and one metre, the form of most praise poems.
A book read aloud in gatherings that tells of our Beloved Prophet's ﷺ blessed birth in prose and verse.
The country of al-Busiri ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, where he lived and is buried, in Alexandria.
Al-Busiri's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ Burdah ends every verse on this letter, so it is also called "al-Mimiyyah".
Al-Busiri's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ second great praise poem, rhyming on the hamzah.
The Companion poet who wrote "Banat Su'ad" after first being against Islam, then came to accept it.
The Companion poet, one of the Ansar, who also answered the poets of Quraysh, alongside Hassan ﵁.
items.a: 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah or Ka'b ibn Malik ⁨(رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا)⁩

items.q: The Blessed Mawlid by Ja'far al-Barzanji ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, read across the Muslim world, is known by this name.
Ja'far al-Barzanji ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, author of the famous Blessed Mawlid, was the Shafi'i mufti of this city.
The Blessed Mawlid written by 'Abd al-Rahman al-Dayba' ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, a hadith scholar of Zabid.
The land of Zabid, the town of al-Dayba' ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The Blessed Mawlid "Simt al-Durar" was written by Habib 'Ali al-Habshi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ of this valley in Yemen.
The poet called "Amir al-Shu'ara'" who wrote "Nahj al-Burdah" in the 20th century CE.
Al-Busiri ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ wrote the Burdah while suffering from this illness, by his own account.
By al-Busiri's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ own account as reported, he was cured after a dream in which our Beloved Prophet ﷺ did this.
items.a: Wiped him or covered him with his cloak

The Burdah of al-Busiri ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ has about this many verses.

items.q: A poem that answers an older one in the same metre and rhyme, like Shawqi's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ "Nahj al-Burdah".
Turning each verse of a poem into five lines by adding three new lines before it.
The Hadrami scholar whose Diwan and litany "al-Ratib" are read daily in Hadramawt and beyond.
The Hanbali poet of Baghdad, famous for praise poems of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ, killed when the Mongols took Baghdad in 656 AH / 1258 CE.
The Lebanese-born scholar and judge who gathered thousands of praise poems in al-Majmu'ah al-Nabhaniyyah.
The Blessed Mawlid of al-Barzanji ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ is known in Arabic as "'Iqd al-Jawhar", meaning this.
Al-Busiri ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ was born in this year.
The scholar Ibn Hajar al-Haytami ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ wrote a long commentary on this poem of al-Busiri ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The Egyptian scholar who wrote a famous commentary on the Burdah, studied at al-Azhar.
Al-Barzanji ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ died in this year.
Al-Dayba' ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, author of the Blessed Mawlid, died in this year.
Habib 'Ali al-Habshi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, author of Simt al-Durar, died in this year.
Ahmad Shawqi's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ "Nahj al-Burdah" answers the Burdah of this poet.
The scholar al-Suyuti ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ wrote this short treatise defending the gathering of the Blessed Mawlid.
The Ayyubid-era ruler of Irbil famous for holding a great Blessed Mawlid every year.
The scholar Ibn Dihyah ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ wrote a Blessed Mawlid book for Kokburi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ with this title.
The poem of supplication beginning "Ishtaddi azmatu tanfariji", by Ibn al-Nahwi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
Al-Busiri's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ long poem rhyming on hamzah opens with a question to our Beloved Prophet ﷺ about how the other Blessed Prophets ﵈ could reach his rank; its first words are these.
The Hadrami scholar 'Abdullah al-Haddad ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ died in this year.
Hassan ibn Thabit ﵁ is reported to have lived to about this age, half before Islam and half in it.
The Damascus scholar 'Abd al-Ghani al-Nabulusi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ wrote a long praise poem using one figure of speech in every verse; this kind of poem is called this.
The Burdah's ten parts include the birth, the miracles, the Qur'an, the Night Journey and this battle-themed one.

Ka'b ibn Zuhayr's ﵁ poem "Banat Su'ad" ends every verse on this letter.
Al-Busiri ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ died in about this year.
